chunks: And whoever leaves his country in duty to God will find many places of refuge, and abundance on the earth. And he who leaves his home and becomes an emigre in the way of God and His Messenger, and death overtake him, is sure to receive his reward from God; for God is forgiving and kind.

key_terms.يُهَاجِرْ: migrates or leaves for the sake of God

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for someone who migrates for God's sake but dies during the journey?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah An-Nisa is often linked to the concept of 'Hijrah al-Sughra' (minor migration) for religious preservation, extending beyond the physical move to Mecca to include any departure for God's sake. The promise of 'muraghan' (abundance) is interpreted not merely as material wealth but as spiritual and physical ease, while the assurance of reward for those who die en route underscores the sincerity of intention (niyyah) over the completion of the journey.
